constraints: The platform must support automated code evaluation for multiple programming languages.
The system should handle concurrent users efficiently.
requirements.target_users: Students, competitive programmers, and individuals preparing for coding interviews or ACM competitions.
requirements.data_requirements: The platform must store user profiles, problem data, code submissions, and evaluation results.

tasks.name: Test Code Submission and Evaluation
tasks.description: Perform testing to ensure code submission and evaluation work correctly.

tasks.name: Test User Profiles and Progress Tracking
tasks.description: Perform testing to ensure user profiles and progress tracking work as expected.

tasks.name: Test Leaderboard Functionality
tasks.description: Perform testing to ensure the leaderboard works as expected.

tasks.name: Deploy ACM Problem-Solving Platform
tasks.description: Deploy the platform to a production environment.

T1.implementation_approach: Use a component-based framework to design an intuitive and responsive interface for browsing, searching, and filtering problems.
T1.notes: Focus on user experience and accessibility.

T2.implementation_approach: Develop RESTful APIs to handle CRUD operations for problems, including search and filter functionalities.
T2.notes: Ensure proper validation and error handling.

T3.implementation_approach: Design a normalized schema to store problem details, tags, difficulty levels, and related metadata.
T3.notes: Optimize for search and retrieval performance.

T4.implementation_approach: Create a code editor interface with syntax highlighting, input/output fields, and submission buttons.
data_structures: JSON for user input and output
T4.notes: Ensure real-time feedback and error highlighting.

T5.implementation_approach: Implement a sandboxed environment to execute user-submitted code and compare outputs with expected results.
T5.notes: Ensure security and prevent malicious code execution.

T6.implementation_approach: Design a profile page to display user details, progress, and achievements.

T7.implementation_approach: Develop APIs to manage user data, including profile updates and progress tracking.
T7.notes: Ensure secure handling of user data.

T8.implementation_approach: Design a schema to store user profiles, progress, and achievements.
T8.notes: Ensure scalability for a large number of users.

T9.implementation_approach: Create a leaderboard interface to display top users based on various metrics.

T10.implementation_approach: Develop APIs to calculate and retrieve leaderboard data based on user performance.

T11.implementation_approach: Design an interface to display hints and explanations for problems.
T11.notes: Ensure hints are accessible without revealing full solutions.

T12.implementation_approach: Develop APIs to manage and retrieve hints and explanations for problems.
T12.notes: Ensure hints are tied to specific problems.

T13.implementation_approach: Write unit and integration tests to verify problem library functionality.
T13.notes: Test edge cases and error handling.

T14.implementation_approach: Simulate code submissions and evaluate the correctness of the evaluation system.
T14.notes: Test for security vulnerabilities in the sandbox.

T15.implementation_approach: Verify user profile updates and progress tracking through automated tests.

T16.implementation_approach: Test leaderboard functionality, including sorting, filtering, and real-time updates.
T16.notes: Test for performance under high load.

T17.implementation_approach: Verify the accuracy and accessibility of hints and explanations.
T17.notes: Ensure hints are displayed correctly for each problem.

T18.implementation_approach: Deploy the platform using a cloud provider with CI/CD pipelines for continuous updates.
T18.notes: Ensure scalability and monitor performance post-deployment.

from flask_sqlalchemy import SQLAlchemy

# Initialize the SQLAlchemy object
db = SQLAlchemy()

from app.database import db


class Problem(db.Model):
    __tablename__ = 'problems'

    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True, autoincrement=True)
    title = db.Column(db.String(255), nullable=False)
    description = db.Column(db.Text, nullable=False)
    difficulty = db.Column(db.String(50), nullable=False)
    created_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, default=db.func.now(), nullable=False)
    updated_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, default=db.func.now(), onupdate=db.func.now(), nullable=False)

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"<Problem {self.title}>"

from app.database import db

class User(db.Model):
    __tablename__ = 'users'

    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True, autoincrement=True)
    username = db.Column(db.String(80), unique=True, nullable=False)
    email = db.Column(db.String(120), unique=True, nullable=False)
    password_hash = db.Column(db.String(128), nullable=False)
    created_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, default=db.func.current_timestamp(), nullable=False)
    updated_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, default=db.func.current_timestamp(), onupdate=db.func.current_timestamp(), nullable=False)

    def __repr__(self):
        return f'<User {self.username}>'

from app.database import db

class Solution(db.Model):
    __tablename__ = 'solutions'

    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True, autoincrement=True)
    problem_id = db.Column(db.Integer, db.ForeignKey('problems.id'), nullable=False)
    user_id = db.Column(db.Integer, db.ForeignKey('users.id'), nullable=False)
    code = db.Column(db.Text, nullable=False)
    language = db.Column(db.String(50), nullable=False)
    created_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, default=db.func.now(), nullable=False)
    updated_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, default=db.func.now(), onupdate=db.func.now(), nullable=False)

    problem = db.relationship('Problem', backref=db.backref('solutions', lazy=True))
    user = db.relationship('User', backref=db.backref('solutions', lazy=True))

    def __repr__(self):
        return f'<Solution id={self.id} problem_id={self.problem_id} user_id={self.user_id}>'

# app/routes.py

from app.controllers.problem_controller import problem_blueprint
from app.controllers.user_controller import user_blueprint
from app.controllers.solution_controller import solution_blueprint

def register_blueprints(app):
    """
    Registers all blueprints to the given Flask app.
    
    :param app: The Flask application instance
    """
    app.register_blueprint(problem_blueprint)
    app.register_blueprint(user_blueprint)
    app.register_blueprint(solution_blueprint)

from flask import Flask
from app.database import db
from app.routes import register_blueprints

def create_app():
    app = Flask(__name__)
    
    # Configure the app (example configuration)
    app.config['SQLALCHEMY_DATABASE_URI'] = 'sqlite:///acm_platform.db'
    app.config['SQLALCHEMY_TRACK_MODIFICATIONS'] = False

    # Initialize database
    db.init_app(app)

    # Register blueprints
    register_blueprints(app)

    return app

from app import create_app

app = create_app()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    app.run()

# ACM Problem-Solving Platform

A website designed to help users solve ACM-style programming problems and improve their coding skills.

## Features

- Problem Library: A comprehensive library of ACM-style programming problems categorized by difficulty and topic.
- Code Submission and Evaluation: Allows users to submit code solutions and receive automated feedback on correctness and performance.
- User Profiles and Progress Tracking: Enables users to create profiles, track their progress, and view their problem-solving history.
- Leaderboard: Displays rankings of users based on their problem-solving performance and achievements.
- Hints and Explanations: Provides hints and detailed explanations for problems to help users learn and improve.

## Setup

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
python app.py
```

## Usage

Open http://localhost:5000 in your browser.
